text:
jess: heads-up — we're iterating on the policy/routing telemetry surface and I'm worried about how it lands in the SDKs (py/ts/go). currently the internal proxy injects an X-Redwood-Policy header with JSON payload. should we expose that directly in the high-level clients or keep it internal behind telemetry hooks? :thinking:
chris: agree we need clarity. exposing raw header -> easy for platform work but brittle for SDK users (header casing, parsing changes). also affects console mapping since we rely on canonical keys.
linh: from devex perspective, users want a simple API: client.call({ routePolicy: 'low-latency', quotaKey: 'team-a' }) rather than fiddling with headers. internal proxies could still add headers but SDK should translate to typed params.
maria: backend note — we plan to normalize headers server-side anyway (accept x-redwood-policy, X-Redwood-Policy). we can keep backward compat for 3 months but we'd rather stop parsing arbitrary keys.
sam: what about telemetry? if SDKs parse and surface the policy object, we can attach it to trace/span attributes (OTel). but sampling and PII need guardrails. we shouldn't send raw customer metadata unless opt-in.
jess: proposal: add a new opt-in SDK flag (policyTelemetry: true/false) default false. SDKs add a typed param in calls (routePolicy/quota) and when enabled they populate telemetry and surface a parsed policy on response metadata. when disabled, SDKs pass-through headers but do not attach to telemetry.
linh: sounds reasonable. for ergonomics: in TS we'd add overloads and a small interface:
```ts
interface RoutePolicy { name: string; priority?: number; tags?: string[] }
client.generate(prompt, { routePolicy })
```
and a top-level client option `enablePolicyTelemetry` for whole-app opt-in.
chris: two concerns: bumping major vs minor. If we add optional params and don't change existing call shapes, it's a minor. but changing default behavior (attaching telemetry) must be opt-in to avoid accidental data leaks.
maria: server change: normalize header names and keep legacy parsing until 2026-08-01. we'll also add a small warning in logs when legacy format is received.
sam: telemetry mapping — Console expects flattened keys: policy.name, policy.priority, policy.tags. need to coordinate with console dashboard folks so UI can show policy breakdowns per-route.
jess: okay. rollout plan draft: 1) backend header normalization + warning (this week) 2) SDKs add typed params + opt-in flag (py/ts/go) - PRs this week, release next Tue as minor versions 3) internal canary with platform team and 2 customers with Dedicated (opt-in) for 2 weeks 4) public opt-in release and docs 5) after 8 weeks, warn about deprecation of raw header parsing.
chris: for Go we should avoid large interface churn — provide a small helper: WithRoutePolicy(ctx, policy) that returns a context carrying policy. avoids changing every function signature.
sam: agree. for python: keyword-only arg is fine (`client.generate(prompt, route_policy=...)`). for TS, overloads or options bag fits.
linh: test matrix: unit tests for serialization, e2e with proxy injecting header, and telemetry tests (ensure opt-in prevents export). also update quickstart snippets in docs.
jess: docs/console_mapping: need a mapping doc that shows how policy JSON maps to console fields and sample queries for the dashboard. I'll file a docs ticket.
maria: question about quota attribution: if SDKs set `quotaKey` we should include that in metering payloads unchanged. backend will add `quota.bucket` attribute. confirm?
chris: yes — design: SDKs set `quotaKey` -> request metadata -> metering pipeline picks `quota.bucket`. must add validation on SDK side to reject TODO: too-long keys (>64 chars).
linh: UX: add a console toggle to show only requests with `policy.name == X`. we can use metadata indexing so queries are fast. console folks, pinged in #product to sync later.
dev-bot: reminder: create RFC for policy-telemetry-surface (link: https://r.redwood/rfcs/123)
jess: agreed action items: - maria: land header normalization + warning - chris: review Go helper pattern - linh: PRs for py/ts SDK shapes + docs snippets - sam: telemetry mapping spec + privacy checklist - jess: create RFC and coordinate canary list
chris: timeline check — can we aim for SDK minor releases and backend change next Tue? we have a deploy window.
maria: yes, backend will target Tue morning. I'll add feature flag so normalization is toggleable in prod for quick rollback.
linh: I'll open the SDK PRs today and request reviews. want to include example snippets and migration guide.
jess: awesome. final call: keep `policyTelemetry` opt-in default false and don't change parsing behavior until after the canary completes. :+1:
chris: +1
maria: +1 (will add deprecation note)
sam: +1 (privacy OK)
linh: filing PRs now.

(reacted: chris :thumbsup:, lin h :party_parrot:)
